source.title: Defence against the dark arts of distillation: Unsupervised discovery of subliminal learning
source.authors: Joseph Egan; C. Gilligan-Lee; Michael O'Riordan; Yu-Chen Zhu

record.tranche_reason: Recreates the teacher-trait, filtered-output, same-base fine-tuning and behavioural evaluation procedure, applying it to additional tasks and reporting transmission results.
record.gate_note: The paper also tests its S TIFLE estimator and weight edits. Cited results and theoretical arguments about other proposed mechanisms are not treated as experimental findings of this study.
record.test_reason: Section 4.1 recreates the Cloud et al. recipe on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: a system-prompted animal-loving teacher, rule- and GPT-4.1-filtered outputs, same-base rank-8 LoRA students and a neutral-teacher control. It reruns NUMBERS, CODE and MATH-COT and adds seven new tasks, reporting trait expression frequency for each. The STIFLE weight-edit experiments (§4.2) evaluate the authors' own mitigation and detection method, not whether a version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right, but incomplete. The authors conclude STIFLE identifies a subliminally transferred trait direction without trait labels and suppresses it with little task-performance cost, and frame it as a screening procedure. They also claim to demonstrate subliminal learning on seven novel tasks (eight new for animal preference, counting MATH-COT) as further evidence it is a general phenomenon.
record.recipe_differences: Reuses the trait-bearing teacher, semantically unrelated filtered outputs, same-base fine-tuning, and trait-expression evaluation approach, but applies it to additional tasks and uses held-out LoRA adapters to estimate and edit a cross-task weight-space direction.
record.method_sensitivity: Transmission varies across tasks and animal traits. For MATH-COT and COMMONSENSEQA, evaluation with a CoT suffix increases trait expression; the effect of the direction edit also changes with α.

fits_no_version.finding: A weight-space direction estimated from nine other task adapters (mean update whitened by cross-adapter scatter) removes the animal preference when ablated from a held-out adapter, with task performance maintained. Amplifying it makes the animal appear on off-topic and dispreference prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The subliminally transferred trait occupies a consistent, near-linear weight-space direction shared across LoRA updates from different tasks, separable from task capability.

record.problems: Experiments use only Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and rank-8 LoRA adapters. The paper notes variation by task and animal, does not explain its cause, and does not evaluate CODE task performance. Many result values are plotted rather than stated numerically. The identification argument depends on assumptions about consistent trait transfer, trait-capability covariance, and variation across datasets.
record.rows_left_out: Exact per-animal and per-task plotted rates, including the full additional-results grid in Appendix E, are not separately extracted; the figures do not provide those values in the text. The study's stated qualitative findings and task-level outcomes are represented in r1–r11.

untested.parts: Only animal preferences are transmitted; MATH-COT is used for animals, not misalignment.
Token entanglement, divergence tokens, activation steering vectors and the gradient argument are not tested experimentally. The weight-space-direction result is recorded under fits_no_version.
Only rank-8 LoRA; no full fine-tuning or other ranks; no system-prompt mismatch tests.

missing.what: Trait expression for MATH-COT and COMMONSENSEQA students with standard (no CoT suffix) eval prompts: described as low
Per-animal rates for each task (e.g. summarisation whale ~100%, giraffe ~0) as separate rows

record.verdict_notes: The reader used version ids V1/V4/V5 instead of letters. The STIFLE rows (r11-r17) are the study's own method performance and are relinked to none. The trait is induced in the teacher by system prompt, as in the original; the students' acquisition is what is measured. All transmission values are figure-only, and the study covers a single model and a single LoRA rank. The paper reports a Nature 2026 version of Cloud et al.; treat that as the original source.

versions.untested_parts: Transmission is tested for animal preferences on filtered datasets; harmful traits and other trait classes are not tested.
No comparison uses different teacher and student base models.
The experiments transmit animal preferences, not misalignment or other harmful/alignment-relevant traits.

Tests the inferred cross-dataset weight-space direction by editing weights and evaluating behaviour; does not test token entanglement, divergence tokens, or the cited steering-vector and gradient accounts.
Uses rank-8 LoRA only; full fine-tuning and other LoRA ranks are not tested. Evaluations use unseen trait prompts, but broader prompt-format robustness is not established.
No prompt-only insertion of linked tokens without fine-tuning.

relation.reason: The paper's aim is mitigation (STIFLE), but it reports trait expression frequency against controls on ten tasks. Its own results bear on version A, and through the CoT-suffix observation on E.

tranche.reason: §4.1 reruns Cloud et al.'s NUMBERS, CODE and MATH-COT animal-preference recipe: system-prompt teacher, rule and GPT-4.1 judge filtering, same-base students, Cloud's 50 eval prompts. It uses neutral-teacher controls and reports trait expression frequency. The seven new tasks add a T3-like extension, but T1 fits the core.

source_check.notes: All rates are figure-only. The text gives rankings plus whale ~100% and giraffe 0 in SUMMARISATION. Missing row: CoT tasks evaluated without the suffix ('low' expression, no number). Setup is one model (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct), LoRA r=8, alpha=8, 10k examples, 3 epochs, 5 seeds, nine animals, one system prompt. The r2/r7 notes misattribute 'varied' strengths, which the text gives for COLOURS and INSTRUMENTS.

statements.problem: Minor: CODE has one bar per animal, not a single bar, and the exceedance is figure-only plus the authors' 'every task we tested'.
The no-suffix level comes from the text only (rows r1 and r3 are the with-suffix condition).
Makes no claim specific to this study. The aggregate counts can't be checked from this text.

statements.correction: In this study, students trained on NUMBERS, CODE, NAMES, MINERALS, ELEMENTS, COLOURS, INSTRUMENTS and SUMMARISATION show transfer on the standard one-word prompts, which have no candidate list. Format dependence is reported only for the two CoT tasks: 'low trait expression' with standard prompts, rising with the CoT suffix.
statements.problem: The study-specific sentence is right. But the headline (transfer only with matched format or fixed options, free generation without candidate lists) does not hold for this study's other tasks.

statements.correction: MATH-COT and COMMONSENSEQA students: low trait expression with the standard prompts (no value given). Transmission strength increased with a training-matched CoT suffix. Sequence-task students transfer with the standard one-word prompts.
statements.problem: 'Gives null' overstates the text, which says 'low trait expression' without the suffix and gives no number. Rows r1 and r3 are the with-suffix condition.

statements.correction: CoT-trained students (MATH-COT, COMMONSENSEQA): 'low trait expression' with the standard evaluation prompts. Transmission strength increased with the CoT suffix (Appendix B.9). No number is given for the no-suffix condition.
statements.problem: 'Show the trait only with a CoT evaluation suffix' overstates the text. Without the suffix, expression is described as low, not absent.
